chapters.title: It asks before it guesses.
chapters.text: Say what the part is for, in words, with a sketch or a photo. PartBuddy offers concepts based on proven designs, asks about loads, cables and the real sizes of your things, and shows a plan. Nothing is built until you press Go.
points: Questions as cards, with the recommended answer preselected and its reason
Research with sources: data sheets, screw tables, standards
Draw the sizes on squared paper or start from a photo
chapters.alt: A housing in the 3D view next to questions from the assistant with recommended options

chapters.title: Real CAD, built while you watch.
chapters.text: SolidCraft builds editable solid geometry step by step in the 3D view. Click a face, pin a note to it and ask for the change in words, or change a size right in the parameter table. Every step, yours or the assistant’s, can be taken back.
points: Threads, countersinks, snap fits, inserts and nut traps on the face you pick
Visible edges rounded, bed edges chamfered and sizes snapped to your nozzle, without being asked
The sizes you name stay exact, and every refinement can be turned off
Logos from SVG files and text in any installed font, placed, sized and changed right on the part
chapters.alt: A cable clip with a selected face and its name, area and actions

chapters.title: Checked against your printer. After every change.
chapters.text: After every change, PartBuddy checks the part against your printer and material and points at each finding. The assistant sees the result too, and the standards behind the numbers are built in.
points: Build volume, wall thickness, overhangs and bed contact
Fits per material, measured on your printer with three test pieces
ISO screws, nuts and heat-set inserts, sized for printing
Hinges and guides run through their whole range: where parts meet on the way is found before you print
chapters.alt: The ready-to-print check reporting that lid and case are too tight

chapters.title: Straight to the plate.
chapters.text: Every part on its print face, nested on the bed of your printer. Open it in Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer with one click, or export 3MF, STEP and STL. Supports and orientation stay with your slicer.
points: One click to Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer
3MF and STL for printing, STEP for other CAD programs
Parts that do not fit the bed are marked
chapters.alt: An enclosure, its lid and a board laid out on a print bed with its size

standards.insertNote: Seats 1 mm deeper than the insert, bosses with at least 2 mm of wall.
supportFree: Edges facing the bed get a 45° chamfer instead of a fillet
Bridges up to 10 mm, ledges up to 1.5 mm, wider ones become a 45° slope
Lying holes above about 10 mm get a teardrop or flat roof
Snap fits at about 1.4 % strain, with a warning above 2 % for PLA
checks: Walls of at least two lines, 0.9 mm with a 0.4 mm nozzle
Overhangs past your material’s angle, as a hint
At least 25 mm² on the bed
Gaps between parts tighter than the push fit

bento.title: Parts that move
bento.text: Ask for a lid that folds or a carriage that slides. The assistant builds a print-in-place hinge or a dovetail guide with the gap your nozzle needs, and you move it with a slider before anything is printed.
bento.alt: A shallow box whose lid stands half folded on a print-in-place hinge with five knuckles

bento.title: Checked through its range
bento.text: The print check runs every joint to its limits and points at the place where two parts meet too early.
bento.alt: The ready-to-print check reporting that the lid meets the box before the hinge reaches its limit

bento.title: Pull it apart
bento.text: Exploded views along the directions the parts go together, and sections along any axis or flat face.
bento.alt: An enclosure, its lid and a screw pulled apart

bento.title: Watch it go together
bento.text: The assembly plays step by step in the right order, sub-assemblies first, set by the assistant or proposed from the geometry.
bento.alt: The assembly of an enclosure halfway, with the named steps beside it

bento.title: Sketch the sizes
bento.text: Draw it on squared paper and type 40, Ø 8 or R 3. The assistant builds from them.
bento.alt: The sketch sheet with typed dimensions and an M3 hole label

bento.title: Start from a photo
bento.text: It asks for the one size that sets the scale. It never guesses from pixels.
bento.alt: The assistant asking for the length of a box shown in a photo

bento.title: Pin a note to the face
bento.text: Click a face, edge or point and pin a note to it: “this edge R2 instead of R1”. The assistant reads it, the note follows its face through rebuilds, says so if it loses its place, and travels with the design file.
bento.alt: A cable clip with three numbered notes on its faces and edge, listed in the structure tree

bento.title: Versions you can compare
bento.text: Saved before every request. Keep any of them as a milestone, compare it with now or open it as a project of its own.
bento.alt: The versions dialog comparing a named version with the current design

bento.title: Measure your printer
bento.text: Pick a material from the catalog, print three small test pieces and enter what fits. Clearances, holes and overhang then match your printer.
bento.alt: The tolerance assistant with the fit comb, hole plate and overhang staircase rendered by SolidCraft

bento.title: Pick model and effort
bento.text: Per chat. With a Claude plan you see how much of it you have used.
bento.alt: The assistant menu with Claude Code, ChatGPT, local models, model and effort

bento.title: Build around real parts
bento.text: Import STEP and IGES as editable bodies, STL, 3MF and OBJ as meshes.
bento.alt: A housing built around an imported circuit board

privacy.title: Your files stay yours
privacy.text: Projects are plain folders on your computer, sign-ins stay in the Windows credential store, and the app sends no telemetry. Its only call of its own is the update check, and you can turn that off. No account, no cloud of its own.

privacy.title: Your model, your choice
privacy.text: Use your Claude or ChatGPT subscription, or keep everything on your machine with a local model.

models.localNote: PartBuddy finds local servers on this computer and offers only models that can call tools and have at least 16K context.
